instructions: Cleve docs, folders and skills live in workspaces (organizations), and an account can belong to several. Every workspace tool accepts an optional `organization` argument (an org id or exact name). Call cleve_list_orgs first to see the workspaces and which one this client currently targets. If a call fails because no workspace is selected, pass `organization`, or call cleve_switch_org once to save a default for this client. Tools that take a doc ID act on that doc wherever you have access to it, in the workspace it belongs to, so they need no `organization`. cleve_read_note returns the doc's `workspace`: pass it as `organization` to search, list or create related docs beside it. A doc shared with you from a workspace you are not a member of can be read and edited as shared, but that workspace cannot be searched or added to. Every Cleve doc has a URL: https://app.cleve.ai/notes/NOTE_ID. Replace NOTE_ID with the exact doc ID (noteId, id, or _id) returned by a tool or supplied in the active doc context. Public, link-shared, and private docs all use /notes/<noteId>; do not use /share/<noteId> or /user/<slug>/<noteId> for a doc link. Never invent an ID. In chat replies, use a clickable Markdown link when delivering a created doc or when the user asks to open or link a doc; prefer the url returned by the tool. A doc URL does not grant access or make the doc public: existing sharing permissions still apply. Docs and folders in results carry a `url` that opens them in Cleve. When you point the user to a doc or folder, or answer from one, link it with that url as a normal Markdown link, e.g. [Q3 Plan](https://app.cleve.ai/notes/<id>), so they can open the source. Sharing and publishing are separate: email collaborators and link access control who can view or edit a doc; web publishing lists a readable post on the owner's public Cleve profile; marketplace publishing creates an installable template copy. Use cleve_get_note_sharing to inspect access, invitations, requests and activity. Copying or returning a doc URL never changes access. Restricted link access and unpublishing do not revoke other grants or inherited folder access.

tools.name: cleve_update_html_block
tools.title: Update interactive block
tools.description:
Replace the markup of an interactive HTML block (a `html cleve-block` widget) that already exists in a doc. Use this rather than cleve_replace_in_note when rewriting a widget: it takes the whole markup at once, so you never have to match a long unique string.

Identify the block by `index` (0-based, counting only HTML blocks in the order they appear, including any nested in a quote, list or table) or by its exact `title`, which must match one block only. Pass `newTitle` to change its caption.

Sandbox rules the markup must respect:
- Inline <style> and <script> work.
- Data fetching is blocked: fetch, XHR, WebSocket, and beacons all fail. The block cannot reach the network for data.
- Scripts, stylesheets, fonts and images MAY load from https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com, https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/ and https://unpkg.com. Scripts may also load from https://cdn.tailwindcss.com and https://code.jquery.com, and Google Fonts stylesheets work. Everything else is blocked by the Content Security Policy, including jsDelivr's /gh/ path, esm.sh and skypack.
- Load libraries as classic `<script src>` builds, or as `<script type="module">` imports from jsDelivr's /+esm URLs. React works either way, but plain DOM code is usually simpler.
- Pin an exact version in every CDN URL (react@18.3.1, never react or react@18), so a new release cannot change or break the block.
- Images may also load from Cleve's own file storage: reuse the link of an image already in the doc or one Cleve generated (it contains /api/storage/).
- Don't inline images, fonts or files as base64 data: URIs; a block that does is refused. Use a storage or CDN link, or draw with SVG or CSS. A tiny icon is fine.
- Keep the whole block under 100 KB of markup.
- The block sizes itself; do not set a fixed body height.
